Work.description: During my role as the first undergraduate Teaching Assistant for the graduate-level Natural Language Processing course at the University of Minnesota, I aimed to bridge the gap in technical expertise among students and enhance their academic experience. I meticulously crafted a 12-week plan that progressively advanced students’ skills in PyTorch and NLP, from foundational concepts to critical research analysis and conference preparation. My approach included designing introductory tutorials, facilitating advanced coding workshops, leading research paper discussions, and organizing industry guest lectures. This experience honed my leadership, technical, and communication skills, enabling me to effectively mentor students and foster a collaborative learning environment. Through this role, I not only assisted in course delivery but also significantly enriched my own academic and professional capabilities, preparing for leadership roles in academia and industry.

projects.description: Inspired by my experiences as a note-taker and tutor, I embarked on developing Gopher Notes, a web platform aimed at enhancing academic collaboration at the University of Minnesota. With a fellow computer science major, we created a prototype that enables students to share course materials and features a points-based leaderboard to encourage contributions. Throughout the process, we streamlined our team from 15 to just two members, realizing the efficiency of smaller, focused groups. Employing technologies like TypeScript, React, Rust, and MySQL, we developed a system that supports student learning and course selection. Now, as we refine our platform based on beta testing feedback, we're on track for a full launch in September 2024, ready to transform how students collaborate academically.
projects.name: Gophernotes
